trickyParts: A section block carries its words in a nested object (text: {type: mrkdwn, text: ...}), so the walk must descend into a display name whose value is not a string. One ordered key list handles both: a string under a display name is taken, any value that is not a string is descended into, in display rank and then alphabetically, so the section's own text precedes its fields and a button's label its hidden value.

Equality dedupe keeps a set of the pieces already taken rather than searching the collected text. The set is created lazily and is bounded by the collection stop, since only a piece that is appended is added to it.

The rich_text exception is keyed on the message's own text holding a non-whitespace character, the same test take() uses to decide that a piece holds a word, so a message whose own text is only whitespace still has its rich_text blocks read.
The committed claude-envoy plugin bundle mirrors skills/, and the required 'Check the committed bundle is fresh' CI step (bun run check-dist) fails if the skill file is edited without rebuilding it.
deviations: The repeat rule is exact equality: a piece is skipped only when it is exactly equal to a piece already taken, the message's own text counted among them, which is what approved spec version 11 states. Beside it one named exception: a message that carries words of its own does not have its rich_text blocks read, since that tree is the Slack client's structured copy of those same words. This is the architect's ruling of 2026-10-25T04:55:00Z (Envoy message d2bf744d502b32e22f038606045cd18b to notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-180-implementer), which withdrew its earlier containment decision (message 2283f04bcf184186ab5c6990da702222) after the reviewer drove containment deleting whole field values — own text '<@U0LEG> page: incident 4213' with fields Severity=1 and Hosts down=2 lost both values, because each occurs inside 4213. It is a return to the approved comparison rule, so no new spec version. No entity-aware comparison was added: the double delivery of a message whose author typed &, < or > disappears because the client's copy is never read.

The order inside one object, also the architect's ruling in the same message: an object's keys are ordered once — the display names in the rank pretext, author_name, title, text, value, footer, fallback, then the remaining keys alphabetically — and that one order is followed whether a value is taken or descended into. Round 1 took the seven display strings first and then descended the remaining keys alphabetically, which put a section's fields before its own text and a button's hidden value before its label.

The three departures the plan recorded stand as the architect accepted them in round 1: the order inside one object is Slack's display order (Go's decoded map keeps no key order), the guard cases cannot fail before the change, and T4 edits skills/legion-controller/references/slack-mentions.md as well as the changelog. The regenerated claude-envoy bundle copy of that skill file is the one file beyond T4's two, and it is generated rather than written.

The reviewer's Security[prompt] finding on fallback and a button's value is not fixed in this pull request: the architect ruled that the approved seven fields stay and that it is taking the question to the human itself. It stands in the pull request body's 'Not proven / risk' list and is answered as 'declined here' on its thread.
